notes:
MIDI controllers, step 4: your Ableton Push 1 now runs AudioLab. The 8 knobs move the selected device (names and values on the Push's display; < and > for more, the arrows pick the device and the track), or the volume or pan of 8 tracks; the buttons under the display select and arm tracks (Mute and Solo switch them); Play, Record, Stop, Metronome, Tap tempo, the tempo and master knobs, Undo (Shift: redo), New, Duplicate, Delete and Quantize work; on a drum kit track the lower left pads play its 16 pads and the top two rows are a 16-step sequencer for the chosen pad.
Behind the scenes for the new meters and analysers: one shared base for scales, units, colour maps and meter speeds. Two fixes you can see: the meter's Loudness reading (Settings, Level meters) is now truly K-weighted like the loudness meter, and the Sidechain device shows its picture again.
Settings, step 4: behind the scenes, every setting in the Settings window is now listed once in one table (page, block, default, help, search words), the base for the coming steps. Nothing looks different.
New: the Kick and bass lab (main menu, or the command list). It shows the note your kick settles on and the bass notes of a bar on one ruler in the song's key, marks where they beat against each other, and fixes it in one click: tune the kick to the root, or move the bass down an octave.
MIDI controllers, step 3: Ableton Push 1 support. Plug in your Push 1: its display shows the track, key and octave, the pads play the selected track in the project key (in key or chromatic, fourths, thirds or in a row), coloured from the track, and Scales on the Push changes key, layout, velocity, pressure and the touch strip.
Behind the scenes for the kick and bass tuning lab: AudioLab can now read which note your kick settles on (exactly for the Kick designer and drum machine kicks, measured for kick samples) and how each bass note of a bar sits against it, in tune or beating. The view that shows it comes next.
Settings, step 3: the Mono and L↔R buttons on the master strip now light up when you change them in Settings; Settings shows all six ways to follow the playhead (Look ahead and Push at the edge too) and the 'Follow again 3 s' switch; the visualizer's own buttons and Settings stay in step.
MIDI controllers, step 2: the Controllers window (menu) is now the full mappings page: see the last message a controller sent, filter by device, set a range, knob kind and speed per mapping, switch feedback, learn a mapping again, and choose the defaults for new mappings.
